definition: A small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
sentence: We put one seed in each pot and added water.

definition: A usually flat, green part of a plant that uses light to help make food.
sentence: There is a small insect under this leaf.

definition: To become bigger as a living thing develops.
sentence: These plants grow quickly beside the sunny window.

definition: A place that gives protection from bad weather or danger.
sentence: The thick hedge provides shelter for small birds during storms.

definition: The kind of place where a plant or animal normally lives.
sentence: Our pond is a habitat for insects and frogs.

definition: To watch something carefully in order to learn about it.
sentence: We observe the birds from a distance and record what they do.

definition: A group of closely related living things recognised as one kind.
sentence: The survey recorded six species of butterfly, although some were seen only once.

definition: Living things and their physical surroundings, considered together with their connections.
sentence: A pond is an ecosystem in which changes to the water can affect many living things.

definition: To protect a natural resource or use it carefully so it remains available.
sentence: The garden club collects rainwater to conserve the school's drinking water.

definition: The variety of living things, including differences within species and among ecosystems.
sentence: Planting several native species may support biodiversity, but the class will monitor which organisms actually appear.

definition: The capacity of a living system to withstand disturbance or recover while retaining its main functions.
sentence: The pond's resilience depends on more than its appearance immediately after a dry summer.

definition: A relationship in which different living things or systems depend on one another.
sentence: The display illustrates interdependence: protecting one species may require attending to relationships that a simple animal count overlooks.

definition: The part of a device that shows pictures or text.
sentence: Touch the picture on the screen to open the story.

definition: To store work on a device so you can use it again.
sentence: Please save your drawing before you close the app.

definition: To look for information by entering words into a digital tool.
sentence: You can search for a book by typing its title.

definition: A piece of equipment made for a particular purpose.
sentence: This small device measures the temperature beside our plants.

definition: A part of a device that detects a condition, such as light or movement.
sentence: The robot stops when its sensor detects an object in front of it.

definition: A planned test used to investigate a question or idea.
sentence: In our experiment, we compared how quickly ice melted in two different places.

definition: A quantity or condition that can change or be changed in an investigation.
sentence: We changed one variable, the amount of light, while keeping the pots and soil the same.

definition: An early version of a design made so its ideas can be tested.
sentence: Our cardboard prototype helped us test the bridge's shape before building a stronger version.

definition: Working consistently well enough to be depended on for a particular purpose.
sentence: We repeated the measurements to check whether the sensor was reliable under the same conditions.

definition: An ordered set of instructions for completing a task or solving a problem.
sentence: The recommendation algorithm favours popular books, which may make less familiar authors harder to discover.

definition: Able to be produced again when the stated procedure and conditions are followed.
sentence: The class documented its instructions carefully so the computer-generated chart would be reproducible.

definition: To estimate beyond the available observations by extending a pattern found in them.
sentence: We should not extrapolate a robot's success on an empty classroom floor to a crowded corridor without examining the new conditions.

definition: To use something belonging to someone else and return it later.
sentence: You can borrow this library book for two weeks.

definition: To ask someone to come to an event or join an activity.
sentence: Let's invite the new student to join our game.

definition: To use or enjoy something together with other people.
sentence: Our groups share the art room on Fridays.

definition: A person who chooses to help with an activity without being paid.
sentence: A volunteer helped us organise the books for the school swap.

definition: A set of questions used to collect information from a group of people.
sentence: The class survey asked which lunchtime clubs students wanted to try.

definition: The opportunity or ability to enter a place or use something.
sentence: Keeping the library open at lunch gives more students access to its books.

definition: To speak or act on behalf of a person or group.
sentence: Council members should listen to classmates with different views if they want to represent them fairly.

definition: A suggested plan presented for people to consider.
sentence: Our proposal explains how a quiet reading corner could share the room with other activities.

definition: An agreement reached when people each adjust some of what they wanted.
sentence: The clubs reached a compromise by using the hall on alternate weeks.

definition: Broad agreement within a group about a view or course of action.
sentence: A consensus emerged in favour of the garden, although members still disagreed about its design.

definition: Responsibility for explaining decisions and answering for their results.
sentence: Publishing the council's decisions supports accountability only if students can also ask how those decisions were reached.

definition: Careful consideration and discussion before a judgement or decision.
sentence: The panel's deliberation became more useful when it examined what each candidate had enabled others to achieve, rather than rewarding confidence alone.
